rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Electric charge is a fundamental, quantized ($q = ne$), and conserved property of matter. Objects can be charged by triboelectric friction, conduction, or electrostatic induction. Charging by induction polarizes mobile electrons in an insulated conductor; momentary grounding allows electron exchange with Earth, permanently trapping an opposite net charge on the conductor without losing inducing charge.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
F = k q₁q₂/r²
E = F/q
∮E·dA = Q/ε₀

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ coulomb: f = (1/4πε₀)·q₁q₂/r². electric field e = f/q = kq/r²; for a line/dipole use superposition..  ·  Thinking induction creates new charge: Induction does not generate charge from nothing; it redistributes existing mobile valence electrons within the conductor while preserving net charge conservation of the combined system.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Grounding must be removed BEFORE withdrawing the inducing charged body; otherwise, mobile charges equalize back through ground, leaving the sphere neutral.  ·  Repulsion is the only sure test of electrification because an uncharged body can be attracted by a charged body due to electrostatic polarization.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Worked: identify given → pick sub-concept → apply standard form → check units / edges.  ·  Electrostatic precipitators: Industrial smoke stacks ionize airborne fly ash and soot particles, which are attracted to grounded collecting plates, purifying factory exhaust by over 99%.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Quantization check: divide given charge Q by 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; if n is not an integer, the charge is physically impossible.  ·  Induction charge sign: Induced net charge on conductor is ALWAYS opposite to the sign of the inducing rod.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Quantization and conservation of electric charge.  ·  Step-by-step mechanism of electrostatic induction and earthing.  ·  Origin of triboelectric series and conduction charge sharing.  ·  Gold-leaf electroscope working and repulsion as the sure test of electrification.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: • Electric charges  ·  Electric charge is quantized in integral multiples of $e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$.  ·  Charge is an isolated invariant scalar conserved across all nuclear and electromagnetic interactions.  ·  Induction charges a conductor with the sign opposite to that of the inducing charged body without contact loss.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Coulomb: F = (1/4πε₀)·q₁q₂/r². Electric field E = F/q = kq/r²; for a line/dipole use superposition.  ·  Gauss's law: ∮E·dA = Q_enc/ε₀ — powerful for spherical/cylindrical/planar symmetry.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Photocopier (Xerography): An aluminum drum coated with photoconductive selenium is charged by corona wire in the dark; light from the document discharges illuminated areas, leaving an electrostatic latent image that attracts toner powder.  ·  Electrostatic spray painting: Paint droplets are given a uniform negative charge as they leave the nozzle, while the metal car frame is grounded/positive. Mutual repulsion atomizes the spray into a fine mist that wraps uniformly around the car.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Nature of charge.** Charge is the property that produces electric force; like charges repel and unlike attract, and the SI unit is the coulomb (C).  ·  **Quantisation and conservation.** Charge is quantised in units of e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (q = ne) and is conserved — the net charge of an isolated system never changes.  ·  **Conductors and insulators.** Conductors (metals) allow charge to move freely, while insulators hold charge in place; excess charge resides on the outer surface of a conductor.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: V = kq/r  ·  Quantization of electric charge: $q = \pm n e \quad (n \in \mathbb{Z}^+)$  ·  Conservation of electric charge: $\sum q_{\text{initial}} = \sum q_{\text{final}}$

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Charge sharing between identical conducting spheres in contact: $q' = \frac{q_1 + q_2}{2}$  ·  Fractional quark composition of nucleon: $p = uud \; (+1e), \quad n = udd \; (0)$  ·  Grounding neutralizes electrostatic potential by allowing electron exchange with Earth's infinite charge reservoir.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Electrostatic attraction occurs between unlike charges and between any charged body and a neutral conductor via polarization.  ·  Believing grounding always pulls electrons down to Earth: If a positively charged rod is inducing negative charge near it, grounding pulls electrons UP from the Earth into the conductor. If a negative rod is near, electrons flow DOWN into the Earth.  ·  Assuming insulators can be charged permanently by induction: Only materials with delocalized mobile charges (conductors) can be charged by induction and grounding. Insulators experience only molecular dielectric polarization.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Remember that in conductors, only negative charges (free conduction electrons) physically move; positive ionic cores remain fixed in the crystal lattice.  ·  Statement 1: Electric charge is quantized, meaning it exists only in integral multiples of the fundamental charge e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.  ·  Statement 2: The total electric charge of an isolated system remains constant over time regardless of physical or chemical reactions.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Statement 3: Electrostatic induction allows charging a conductor with a sign opposite to that of the inducing charged object without physical contact.  ·  Statement 4: Repulsion is the definitive test of electrification, since neutral matter is attracted to any charged body by polarization.  ·  Statement 5: Charge is invariant under relativistic transformations, independent of the relative velocity of the frame of reference.
